I am a licensed Loan Officer and recently ran into an audit finding with UWM on a previous client. This part is information prior to my loan which I believe can be beneficial to the entire complaint. The audit team asked for documents and proof of the properties being rented to offset his XXXX so the outcome of his approval wouldn't change. About a week later they notified us that he has been black listed for undisclosed properties after the property had been sold and the loan paid in full. I relayed the information to him with their decision. It turns out that the other properties were with UWM as well through a different Loan officer in another state. UWM ( United Wholesale Mortgage ) systems for checks and balances should have triggered or caught this in my opinion. If all of his info is on each property how did UWM not catch thi s prior to them closing back to back? This shows severe issues in the UWM system process which puts the consumer at risk. Not to mention it puts UWM at risk as well. This is when things really started showing up at my door step. A few months later I needed to refinance my own property. I started to notice or feel that I was being targeted and wondered if I myself had been flagged due to the previous incident. In a nutshell I was pushed over to having a higher rate and payment do to negligence of the UWM team. We clearly know this is illegal and is a ploy for UWM to make more money with me being at a higher rate. At closing I signed the anti steering document as there was no steering by XXXX Mortgage, I feel confident that there was steering by the underwriters to push me into products that would have been more beneficial for the company. I will explain this further below as I explain the series of events. On another occasion the underwriter requested a CPA letter. I gladly reached out and copied the exact request from underwriting that I received from the processor and sent it over to my CPA. United Wholesale Mortgage is currently processing a loan application for a mutual client and we were provided a CPA explanation letter on your letterhead and bearing your signature. Your assistance is appreciated. Please feel free to reach out directly with any questions or concerns. It appears this was perfectly set up to try and entrap me and again to deny the loan. The font in the letter is slightly different. However, there is a repeated trend in how my account is being handled by UWM. This appears to be Overt Evidence and a violation of fair lending. Let 's move on to credit accounts with installments less than 10 months. UWM refused to make changes though statements proved that there were less than 10 months. As defined under Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) Fair Debt Collection Practices Act as well as the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), it is required that all accounting be applied based on actual amounts that are due. I have been paying an extra {$600.00} to {$700.00} per month towards negative escrow, which has not been applied accordingly. The monthly statements issued by SLS show that the minimum monthly payments due are {$1600.00}. The principal payment is {$200.00}, with interest being {$360.00} per month, which leaves the balance {$1000.00} to be applied to escrow ( ex B ). The {$1000.00} has not been applied towards escrow due, instead it has been held in suspense accounts and re-allocated. Per CFPB rule 1026.41, the amount due, has shown more prominently than other disclosures on the page and, if the transaction has multiple payment options, the amount due falls under each of the payment options and CFPB rule. Furthermore, the rule states that the monthly payment amount, including a breakdown showing how much, if any, will be applied to principal, interest, and escrow and, if a mortgage loan has multiple payment options, a breakdown of each of the payment options along with information on whether the principal balance will increase, decrease, or stay the same for each option listed must be shown. Since there is a lack of transparency in the negative escrow accounting, we are requesting that all payments be reallocated and applied to the negative escrow amount currently listed as {$21000.00}. CFPB Rule 1024.17 also has standards listed that must be adhered to in relation to escrow. if a servicer advances funds for a borrower, then the servicer must perform an escrow account analysis before seeking repayment of the deficiency. Proper analysis is not being performed to bring the escrow account out of delinquency.
